chunks: Al-Kafi: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, all together, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abi Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
It is not proper for the girl if she has begun menstruating to not veil herself, unless she cannot find it.

key_terms.تَخْتَمِرَ: she veils herself/wears a head covering

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a girl's hijab after she starts menstruating?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi clarifies the onset of legal modesty requirements for girls upon menstruation, emphasizing that covering the body is obligatory unless a covering garment is genuinely unavailable. It reflects the Shia juristic principle that the duty of hijab is contingent upon the capacity to fulfill it, linking physical maturity directly to religious accountability.
